Newtown Hospital

Dear Doctor,
Re: Ms Sally McConville,     aged: 38
I am writing to request an urgent assessment and management of Ms McConville, who is                 Commented [OET2]: Assessment is countable and
presenting with acute exacerbation of her asthma with superimposed pneumonia.                        uncountable; however, using an article is better in this
                                                                                                     context
                                                                                                     Commented [OET3]: Pneumonia diagnosis is not yet
                                                                                                     confirmed
In terms of Ms McConville’s medical history, she has asthma which is managed by fluticasone and
Ventoline.


Initially, Ms McConville presented to me on 10/09/2014 with a 2-day history of a runny nose, fever
and a productive cough. She had nasal congestion, redness of the throat and scattered chest
wheezes on examination. Hence, I suspected a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract and
prescribed medications accordingly. Subsequently, Ms McConville revisited yesterday with
shortness of breath, yellowish sputum and fever of [at] 38*C. Therefore, amoxicillin 500 mg and
prednisolone 25 mg were added with her previous medications.                                         Commented [OET4]: to




Today, Ms McConville presented again with deterioration of her condition. She had a respiratory
rate of 25, widespread wheeze, bibasal crepitations and obvious use of accessory muscles for
breathing. Hence, I nebulized her with 5 mg of Ventoline[no space]; however, her condition
showed no improvement.


In view of the above, I would appreciate your immediate attention for management of her
condition. Please, do not hesitate to contact in case of any queries.


Yours sincerely,
Doctor
